classes.name: Országgyűlési képviselők választása
classes.finest_note: Votes are published by polling station (szavazókör); postal and foreign-mission votes as separate units.
classes.note: 1990–2010: 386 seats (176 two-round single-member constituencies, up to 152 seats on 20 territorial lists, and at least 58 national compensation seats; Act XXXIV of 1989). Since 2014: 199 seats (106 first-past-the-post constituencies and 93 national-list seats, with preferential nationality lists; Act CCIII of 2011). Parliamentary by-elections are held in the single-member constituencies.

cadence.day_rule: a Sunday in April or May of the fourth year after the previous election
cadence.runoff_rule: Single-member constituencies: an absolute majority on a valid first round (turnout over half) elects; otherwise a second round two weeks later (Act XXXIV of 1989, § 7).

cadence.day_rule: a Sunday in April or May of the fourth year after the previous election
cadence.vacancy_rule: A vacant single-member seat is filled by a by-election (időközi választás) unless the term ends within the year; a vacant list seat passes to the next candidate on the list.

classes.name: Társadalombiztosítási önkormányzati választás
classes.note: Insured persons elected the employee side of the Health Insurance and Pension Insurance self-governments from union lists in one nationwide vote; Parliament abolished the self-governments in 1998.
classes.disposition_reason: The National Election Office's archive does not hold the 1993 vote, and no official machine-readable or tabulated return by area has been found; only the national result was announced.

classes.name: Testületek által választott tisztségek
classes.name_en: Offices filled by assemblies and councils
classes.disposition_reason: Chosen by an assembly, not by voters: the Prime Minister, the Speaker, Constitutional Court judges, and the Kúria president (by the National Assembly), county assembly presidents and deputy mayors (by the councils), and lay judges (by local councils).

classes.name: Bírák
classes.disposition_reason: No judicial office is filled by popular vote: professional judges are appointed by the President, and lay judges are elected by local councils (see kozvetett).

classes.name: Előválasztás
classes.disposition_reason: The electoral procedure act (Ve. § 1) covers no nominating contest; parties pick candidates themselves, and the 2021 opposition primary was run by the parties, not the election office.

classes.name: Köztestületi és kamarai választások
classes.disposition_reason: Run by the chambers themselves among their members (economic, agrarian, and professional chambers), not by the election office under the electoral procedure act.

classes.name: Vármegyei közgyűlés választása
classes.finest_note: Voters outside the county-rank towns vote for county lists; published by polling station.
classes.note: In 1990 the county assemblies were elected indirectly by electors of the municipal councils; directly from county lists since 1994 (1994–2006 in two sections, settlements up to and over 10,000).

classes.name: Országgyűlési (képviselőházi és nemzetgyűlési) választások 1848–1939
classes.name_en: Diet, House of Representatives, and National Assembly elections, 1848–1939
classes.note: Census-suffrage elections to the lower house of the diet from 1848 (413 constituencies from 1875), then the National Assembly of 1920 and 1922 and the House of Representatives of 1926–1939, partly by open ballot. Elections ran over several days; dates are the month the voting began. Constituency returns are in the Parliament's almanacs and, from 1920, KSH's election statistics volumes.

access.evidence: Scanned KSH election statistics volumes with constituency returns; no machine-readable file.

classes.name: Felsőház
classes.disposition_reason: Members sat by birth, office, or appointment, or were chosen by county and municipal assemblies and professional bodies; no popular vote.

classes.name: Törvényhatósági és községi választások
classes.name_en: County, municipal, and village assembly elections before 1950
classes.note: Half of each county and municipal committee (törvényhatósági bizottság) sat by virtue of paying the most tax (virilisták); the other half was elected by constituency.
classes.disposition_reason: Each county and town ran its own elections and no national compilation of returns by an official body is known; returns survive only in county archives.

classes.name: Nemzetgyűlési és országgyűlési választás 1945, 1947
classes.note: List PR in county constituencies plus a national list; 409 seats in 1945 and 411 in 1947.

access.evidence: Scanned KSH election statistics with settlement returns.

classes.name: Országgyűlési választások a Népköztársaságban
classes.name_en: National Assembly elections of the People's Republic
classes.note: Single Patriotic People's Front list in 1949 and 1953 (county lists), single-member constituencies from 1967 with one nominee in most, and compulsory multiple nomination in 1985 with second rounds.

access.evidence: National and county totals in KSH yearbooks; constituency returns from 1967 in scans.

dates.note: Second round where no candidate won a majority on 8 June.

classes.name: Tanácsválasztások
classes.name_en: Council elections of the People's Republic
classes.note: County, town, district, and village councils elected on Patriotic People's Front nominations, usually on the same day as the parliamentary election from 1958.

access.evidence: National and county totals only.
